17.0.0.en: Six days after informing them of the news of His sufferings and death, Christ went up with three of His close disciples, whom He had chosen to accompany Him at the raising of the daughter of Jairus, and to enter with Him into the depths of the Garden of Gethsemane before His arrest, because of their spiritual readiness to understand lofty matters more than the rest. For He wants to reveal everything to everyone, but not everyone wants to understand, and these had greater love for Him.

17.0.1.en: "Six": this number signifies the completion of human work, but it is less than the number seven, which is the completion of the divine work by the Holy Spirit. When a person completes what he is able to do of striving, the grace of God reveals to him the divine help. The Transfiguration was to support the disciples, so that they would not be wearied and doubt when they saw His crucifixion and death. And He took the three because "in the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established", and they represent all mankind, like the three sons of Noah.

17.0.2.en: He took them up on a high mountain, since it is necessary, with toil, to rise above limited earthly thinking in order to ascend to heavenly things, so that God may reveal Himself to us.

17.1.0.en: Christ revealed some of the brightness of His divinity, as much as His three disciples could bear, for the greatest light they know is the sun, and so His face became, for He is the Sun of Righteousness who lights our lives. As for His garments, they became white as the light, and garments are what cling to the body, so they signify the Church that is enlightened by Christ.

17.2.0.en: Moses appeared, who represents the Law, and Elijah, who represents the prophets, because in Christ the Law and the prophecies of the prophets are fulfilled, and to confirm that He fulfills the Law and establishes all the teachings of the prophets. Moses died and then appeared in a spiritual body, whereas Elijah ascended in his body and came to appear in this Transfiguration. For Christ is the God of the living and the dead, because the spirits of those who died are kept with Him.

17.2.1.en: Moses and Elijah spoke of the redemption which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem (Lk 9:31), for it is the goal of the Law and the prophets, that is, the salvation of the world, and the disciples probably knew the persons of Moses and Elijah from Christ's calling them and speaking with them. The following appears from the Transfiguration:

17.2.2.en: (1) That those who have fallen asleep, like Moses, are still alive with God.

17.2.3.en: (2) That the spirits in heaven know one another.

17.2.4.en: (3) That the saints in heaven care about our salvation.

17.3.0.en: The disciples rejoiced greatly at this divine sight, and enjoyed seeing Moses and Elijah, and wished that this sight would not end.

17.3.1.en: And from his joy and admiration at the greatness of this Transfiguration, Peter rushed forward as was his habit, and expressed the feelings of the disciples by proposing to Christ the making of three tabernacles, so that they might remain a longer time in this place; and he did not understand that these spiritual beings do not need tabernacles to shelter them.

17.4.0.en: While Peter was dazzled and attached to the sight of the Transfiguration, Christ saw that they could not bear to see His divinity more than this, so a bright cloud came, signifying the luminous indwelling of God, and Christ, Moses, Elijah and the three disciples disappeared inside it. And in this fearful sight inside the cloud, they heard a voice from heaven declaring that Christ is the beloved Son, to whom all people must submit and listen; for the Father testifies that Christ is the Son of God, the Only-Begotten Son.

17.5.0.en: The disciples were greatly afraid when they entered the cloud and no longer saw anything, neither Christ nor Moses and Elijah, nor each one his two companions. And before the awe of the Father's voice from heaven, they fell on the ground in their weakness as human beings, but Christ the Redeemer is able to raise them from earthly things to heavenly things.

17.6.0.en: Christ touched His disciples, and so supported and encouraged them, and they rose to find that the sight of the Transfiguration had ended, and Jesus, whose appearance they were accustomed to, standing alone with them in His ordinary human form.

17.6.1.en: By this, the Holy Bible confirms that one thing is needful, which is looking to Christ our God and Savior.

17.7.0.en: Christ charged them not to tell the rest of the disciples or the multitudes of the sight of the Transfiguration until after His resurrection from the dead, because the hearers would not believe, and it would stir up the scribes and Pharisees against them, as they would appear before them as liars, claiming things that in their view were not true. And if some believed their words, this might lead them to confirm the idea of the earthly kingship they long for, so that they would move away from the spiritual, heavenly kingship that Christ intends.

17.7.1.en: But after the resurrection, the sight of the Transfiguration would support His divinity, and they would be assured of it even more after the Holy Spirit came upon them, that is, with the help of God.

17.7.2.en: Christ is ready to be transfigured before you if you desire it, indeed He is being transfigured in fact, but you may not notice it because of your many material preoccupations. He speaks to you through the Holy Bible and the guidance of the Church, and even through the events of life and the remarks of those around you, and in various ways calls you to repentance and to knowing Him and living with Him. And the more attentively you listen, the more His appearing to you increases in simple, clear ways, and you enjoy fellowship with Him always.

17.8.0.en: As the three disciples were coming down from the mountain with Christ, and this was at dawn, since the Transfiguration probably happened at night, because Luke the Evangelist also mentions that when they came down from the mountain on the next day, that is, after the night had passed (Lk 9:28-37), they asked Christ about what the scribes say, that Elijah must first come again to the earth: was this fulfilled by the Transfiguration of Christ on the mountain, or is it another coming, since Elijah did not die but ascended alive to heaven?

17.8.1.en: And the second coming of Elijah was mentioned in the prophecy of Malachi (Mal 4:5).

17.9.0.en: Christ affirmed that Elijah will come again to call people to repentance, and this will happen immediately before the Day of Judgment, in the midst of the surge of evil, to bring people back to faith, in the last opportunity available to mankind before the judgment.

17.10.0.en: Christ pointed here to the spiritual coming of Elijah, where John the Baptist came with the same character as Elijah, that is, detachment from material things and strength in proclaiming the truth. The Baptist suffered from the opposition of the scribes and Pharisees to him, just as they do to Christ the Son of Man, and the Jews did not know that John had come in the spirit of Elijah, that is, with his same character.

17.10.1.en: "They have done unto him whatsoever they listed": that is, they opposed him and were pleased at his killing, for although the killer was Herod, had it not been for the opposition of the chief priests to him, he would not have been able to kill him because he feared the people.

17.10.2.en: "The disciples understood": the disciples did not understand until He explained to them the details of John's preparing the way for Him, and they knew that the talk was about John who came in the spirit of Elijah.

17.10.3.en: God alerts us to repentance in many ways however evil we are, so may we respond quickly to His calls, for He is a tender Father who will support us and give us strength to reject the enticements of sin.

17.11.s.en: (3) The casting out of the demon that the disciples could not cast out

17.11.0.en: After the divinity of Christ appeared in the Transfiguration, the weakness of Satan appears before Him, as a man came to Him and worshiped Him, asking Him to heal his son who had a demon that throws him on the ground unconscious, and sometimes throws him into the fire or the water to kill him, and they rescue him with difficulty. This represents the wicked person subject to the devil, who loses his peace and balance, and the devil tries to destroy him by throwing him into various lusts.

17.11.1.en: And the man added that the disciples of Christ were unable to cast it out, although they had cast out other demons when He sent them to preach in Judea.

17.12.0.en: Christ rebuked the weakness of faith of His disciples, and the man whose son had a demon, who represents the whole multitude, and He rebuked also their perverseness, that is, their doubt of the power of God and their preoccupation with worldly lusts, because the scribes seized the opportunity of the disciples' inability to cast out the demon, and began to argue with them, showing their helplessness and casting doubt on the standing of their Teacher Jesus.

17.12.1.en: And He rebuked their weakness, because He had left them for a little while, and the weakness of their faith appeared. And this was beneficial for the disciples and for the multitude, so that they would know that the source of their power is Christ, and would always take refuge in Him, and be able to do everything. Then He rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy, who was restored to health.

17.13.0.en: "A grain of mustard seed": the smallest of seeds in size, and it signifies very small faith.

17.13.1.en: After the multitudes departed, the disciples asked Christ why they were unable to cast out this demon, and He assured them that the reason was their unbelief, and He showed that the power of faith, however small, can move a mountain; and this actually happened in the moving of the Mokattam mountain in Cairo in the year 970 AD in the time of Anba Abraam ibn Zaraa the Syrian (Pope 62).

17.13.2.en: And what is meant is not only the ordinary mountain, but even more sins and evil lusts, which are harder than ordinary mountains.

17.14.0.en: Christ declared that to overcome Satan, we need faith that appears in deep prayers, and fasting, because it is detachment from the worldly desires that the devil uses to entice us. Consequently, we rob him of his power and overcome him by the power of God; in addition, fasting shows our love for God more than for food and material things. If God permits your weakness to appear at times, it is so that you may examine yourself and take refuge in Him, and so receive greater strength and advance in your spiritual life, so do not be troubled by weaknesses and falls, but rise quickly, confident that you are the beloved child of God, able by His power to overcome all the power of Satan.

17.15.s.en: (5) The tribute of the two drachmas

17.15.0.en: The priests of the Jews used to take two drachmas every year from every Jewish person for the needs of the temple, and the drachma at that time was a coin of small value. The tax collectors came to Capernaum and asked Peter about Christ's paying this tax, so that if He did not pay it, regarding Himself as a prophet, they would find a charge against Him that He was against the temple and did not care for its needs, and if He paid the two drachmas, He was an ordinary person and not the awaited Messiah, because the Messiah in their view would possess an earthly kingdom.

17.15.1.en: And this tax is not compulsory from the state, but a sign of the Jew's concern for the service and worship of the temple.

17.16.0.en: "Yes": that is, yes, and so agreement to pay the tax.

17.16.1.en: Christ knew of the conversation that took place between the tax collectors and Peter without hearing it, because He is God who knows everything. So He took the initiative of asking Peter about the collecting of taxes, whether it is from the children (the Jews) or from strangers? Peter said to Him: From strangers. Then Jesus said to him: Then are the children free from paying taxes, that is, Christ is the Son of God and the Lord of the temple, so naturally He does not pay the tax.

17.16.2.en: "Their children": He means the awaited Messiah and the prophets, and no tax is taken from these because they are the owners of the temple. "Strangers": He means the rest of the Jews other than the prophets.

17.16.3.en: Submit to the order that exists in society, even if it is not sound in your view, out of respect for its laws, since your heart is occupied with what is more important, that is, eternity.

17.17.0.en: Because the priests of the Jews did not yet believe, He said to Peter: lest we offend them, I will pay the tax. And Christ directed him to the work he knew, which is catching fish, so he would cast a hook into the sea, and the fish he caught first, he would open its mouth and find in it a stater, which is a coin equal to four drachmas, and he would pay the tax for Christ and for himself.

17.17.1.en: And by this the authority of Christ over animals appears, and His knowledge of the unseen, that is, of the presence of a stater in the mouth of the fish, and then He directs it to come up on the hook.

17.17.2.en: His love and care for His disciple Peter also appear, as He pays the tax for him.

17.17.3.en: And the poverty of Christ and most of His disciples also appears, as He had no money at all, not even a little. Be confident that your God, the Almighty, is able to do everything and meets your needs, so do not be troubled by those who oppose you.

18.0.0.en: The disciples were still thinking of the Kingdom of Heaven in a human way, so they asked to know who is the greatest in heaven. This shows discussions and thoughts within them about who is the greatest among them, and who will be chief in the new kingdom; and the love of chief place is of course a kind of pride.

18.1.0.en: Christ's reply to them was that the greatest is the humble, innocent one who loves everyone. And He gave them His answer in a practical way, for He set a child in the midst of them, and asked them to become like him in humility, innocence and love, for these are the conditions for entering the Kingdom. It is to be noted that He did not answer their question, which was who is the greatest, but declared the conditions for entering the Kingdom, so that it might be understood that with the love of chief place and pride they will not enter the Kingdom.

18.2.0.en: Christ finally answered their question, that the greatest is the humble and innocent one who obeys the commandments of God like this child, and according to the degree of distinction in becoming like children, a person enjoys Christ in eternity.

18.3.0.en: "In my name": that is, for the sake of Christ.

18.3.1.en: On another side, Christ honored childhood, which was neglected at that time by all classes of the world, whether Romans, Greeks or Jews, for He declared that childhood belongs to Him, so whoever receives a child and cares for him and is concerned for him is like one who received Christ Himself, because this receiving means love and tenderness. People are concerned with hosting and receiving the rich, but Christ directs their eyes to receiving the weak, the despised and the needy, because concern for them is concern for Christ.

18.3.2.en: Be concerned, not only for children, but for every person who has no one to look after him or who suffers weakness, for your love offered to him pleases God as if it were offered to Him personally.

18.4.0.en: "Little ones": any person weak in his abilities who can be made to fall into sin, and this includes in truth all the faithful, because all are liable to fall into sin.

18.4.1.en: "The depth of the sea": the fullness of the sea and its depth.

18.4.2.en: A stumbling block is a doubled sin, for a person falls into sin and makes another fall. Stumbling blocks result from the love of worldly lusts, inflexibility, and little feeling for others, especially the weak such as children. Therefore it is a great crime, and whoever insists on causing others to stumble and does not repent must perish, and his perishing is expressed by "that a millstone were hanged about his neck", which is a heavy stone used for crushing grain by being turned over a fixed stone. And when a person tied to this stone is thrown, he will certainly drown in the sea.

18.4.3.en: So if stumbling blocks must exist because of the evil of people, Christ declares that woe awaits the one who causes the stumbling and fall of another, and he is condemned to destruction like one who drowns in the depth of the sea, which signifies worldly lusts, so that his falling into many sins is easy, and he goes away from God.

18.4.4.en: Be careful about your speech, your appearance and your conduct, so that you do not cause the simple to stumble and turn them away from God... for how can you make fall those for whom Christ died, how can you hand them over to sin by your carelessness?!

18.4.5.en: The one who causes another to stumble has had his heart hardened by the lusts of the world, and for this reason his punishment is very severe.

18.5.0.en: "Life": He means our life in the world.

18.5.1.en: "Halt ... maimed ... one eye": that is, to live without the person or thing that you regard as important, like a member of your body such as your foot, your hand and your eye.

18.5.3.en: After speaking of the gravity of causing others to stumble, He warns us not to stumble ourselves and fall into sin, and says that however important the matter, we should be rid of it as long as it causes us to stumble. And He gave comparisons with necessary members of the body such as the foot, the hand and the eye, which signify the important things in our lives; as long as they lead us to evil lusts, let us keep away from them, whether it be a friend or relative or place or a stumbling work or a hobby, or anything the devil uses to make us fall into sin. For it is better for you to live in this earthly life giving up something important, so that you are like the lame or the maimed or the one-eyed, than to hold to what causes you to stumble and makes you fall into sin, and so go to eternal torment.

18.5.4.en: Do not say, I will leave sin and hold on to the evil relationship, since I have already fallen; flee for your life from this relationship, because the salvation of your soul is the most important thing. Do not be careless and cast yourself into eternal torment.

18.5.5.en: Set it in your heart that you must live for Christ forever, so leave behind everything that leads to sin, even if wicked people mistreat you because of your distance from evil. For enduring anything, even death itself, is easier than eternal torment.

18.6.0.en: Here He speaks of caring for others and not causing them to stumble by our carelessness, affirming the value of their souls before God, and He declares an important truth of faith, that each one of us has a guardian angel. These children, or simple or weak ones, their souls have value before God, and they have angels who always pray for them in heaven. On the other hand, Christ came to redeem these despised ones, and the price of the salvation of their souls is His precious blood, which is the greatest thing in existence.

18.6.1.en: Beware of contempt, for if anyone falls because of your carelessness, this grieves God and His angels greatly, and God responds to the intercession of the angels of these people, and raises them from their sins if they repent.

18.7.0.en: "The ninety and nine": they signify the angels who did not fall. It may also be interpreted as those righteous in their own eyes, whom God leaves because they do not feel their need of salvation, and He seeks the one who fell and feels that he is wicked.

18.7.1.en: "Upon the mountains": where there is safety in the folds prepared for it.

18.7.2.en: "That which is gone astray": it is the one who has fallen into sin and feels his weakness. It also signifies all mankind who strayed from God, as distinguished from the angels who did not fall.

18.7.3.en: "He rejoiceth": because he was lost and dead, and he lived and returned to his true life in God by repentance. He shows God's love for those who stumble because of their weakness, by the parable of the man who has a hundred sheep and only one goes astray, for he is not occupied with the ninety and nine, but shuts them in the fold and goes out searching with care until he finds this lost one. For God cares for and seeks every person, however weak or lowly he may seem, until He saves him.

18.7.4.en: Be confident that you have a place in the heart of God that no one else fills, so if you fall, repent quickly, to return to your place and so rejoice and make Him rejoice.

18.8.s.en: (3) Dealing with those who wrong us

18.8.1.en: "Between thee and him alone": privately, so that you do not embarrass him before others, or stir up his pride so that he tries to justify himself.

18.8.2.en: "Thou hast gained thy brother": you have restored your good relationship with him, and at the same time his heart was purified and his relationship with God returned.

18.8.3.en: Christ explains how to deal with one who wrongs you. The first thing is that you love him, and take the initiative to go to him to rescue him from persisting in the fault into which he has fallen. For he has not only troubled you, but has sinned against God and himself, so you go to him in love to reprove him, so as to show him what he has done wrong.

18.8.4.en: He did not say that you rebuke him, because the aim is not to show his faults and prove them against him, or to take your right from him, but the aim is that you win him to Christ, and bring him back to Him by your love for him and your concern for his salvation, so that your manner of speaking is the reproof of love, with gentleness and tenderness.

18.9.0.en: If he refuses to hear your reproof and persists in his fault, do not despair, but take with you one or two of the beloved, especially those known to him, that perhaps by their intercession he may be persuaded to restore good relations with you and remove the causes of the dispute. Then your reproof is not merely your personal opinion, but two or three, whose opinion has more influence. On the other hand, they will be two witnesses against the wrongdoer when the matter is brought to the Church, as Moses commanded in the Law (Deut 17:6).

18.10.0.en: If this second attempt at reconciliation fails, do not despair either, but tell the Church, that is, the priests and servants, so that they may try to persuade him to remove the dispute and restore love. And if he persists in the fault, treat him as you would treat the heathen man and the publican, that is, those far from the Church, so you love him and pray for him, even if relations between you are cut off because of his refusal, or your relationship is limited and not a friendship.

18.11.0.en: The Church supports you in your stand so that you do not blame yourself, for it has the right to bind him, that is, to prevent him from her membership and from receiving the Sacraments, because of his persistence in the fault. But if he returns and repents, it has the right to loose him, and he has communion in the Church, and in heaven also after the end of this life.

18.11.1.en: And here is a second affirmation of the authority of the priesthood in the sacrament of confession, not only for Peter as mentioned in (ch. 16:19).

18.12.0.en: He opens the door of hope for this sinner who persists in his fault, for despite the Church's excluding him, she asks you and everyone who loves him to pray for him until he repents.

18.12.1.en: And He encourages us that the agreement of two in love and prayer is great in the eyes of God, so He gives them their request for the return of this sinner and his repentance.

18.12.2.en: And He affirms the importance of common prayer by the gathering of two or three, for Christ dwells with a special blessing in their midst; He blesses everyone who prays, but there is an additional blessing and a special indwelling of Christ in common prayer, and the greatest common prayer is the prayer of the Divine Liturgy around the Body and Blood of the Lord, and, extending from it, the family's prayer at home, that is, the husband and wife and children, in which they ask for the needs of the home and its cohesion, and it encourages its members to the spiritual life and to love one another.

18.12.3.en: May your love appear, not only toward those who love you, but even more toward those who wrong you, so that you seek them in love to reconcile with them and win their souls. And if all your attempts fail, persevere in praying for them, having compassion on them, and the mercies of God toward you will increase.

18.13.s.en: (4) The extent of forgiveness toward others

18.13.0.en: Peter asked Christ about the extent of bearing the faults of others and forgiving them: should he forgive seven times? And this number is not small, because the Jews in their book "the Talmud" say that forgiveness is three times. It is understood from Peter's question that forgiveness has limits, and he asks about them.

18.14.0.en: Christ answered: "Until seventy times seven", that is, 490 times, and this is a huge number, and what is meant by it is forgiveness without limits, and not thinking about how sincere the wrongdoer is in not returning to the fault.

18.14.1.en: If God asks us to forgive without limits, this reassures us that His mercy is very wide, and His forgiveness is endless too, as long as we repent and return to Him, on condition of not being careless, so that we do not lose the spirit of repentance and leave God.

18.15.0.en: Christ explains the idea of forgiveness without limits toward others, so He likened the Kingdom of Heaven, in which we wish to live, and whose beginning is the Church on earth, to a king (who signifies Christ the Judge) to whom was brought a servant, that is, a sinful person, who owed an enormous sum, ten thousand talents, and to know how huge this sum is, we say that the gold used in the temple of Solomon in all its splendor was eight thousand talents. What is meant is that man's sins against God are enormous, indeed without limit, because God is unlimited and the punishment for a fault against Him is unlimited.

18.16.0.en: The helplessness of this servant appeared, that is, of each one of us who sins against God, and consequently the king's (God's) judgment on him was that he be sold, with his wife and his children, that is, his body and his gifts, perhaps they might pay something of what he owed, but they would be of no use before this very huge debt. By this the weakness and evil of each one of us appears before divine justice.

18.17.0.en: This servant worshiped, asking for patience, that he not be sold, that is, handed over to Satan and eternal torment. And here God's forgiveness of him appears, for He forgave him and released him with his wife and his children, and what is meant, as we mentioned, by his wife is his body, and by his children his gifts. That is, by the blood of Christ the Redeemer our sins were lifted from us, and He gave us renewal for our bodies, our spirits and all our gifts.

18.17.1.en: For God in His tenderness did not only grant the servant's request, which was for patience, but removed the debt from him, because He knows his inability to pay it however much time was given to him.

18.18.0.en: After this servant was freed from his debts, he found a fellow servant, that is, a person who had sinned against him, who owed him a hundred denarii, a very small sum that has no comparison with the ten thousand talents (it equals one to a million and a quarter).

18.18.1.en: "Ten thousand": the number ten signifies the fault of the cruel servant against the Ten Commandments, and the number thousand signifies eternity, that is, that he deserves eternal punishment.

18.18.2.en: And despite the second servant's pleading with the first to have patience with him, the first servant was cruel, and did not forgive or pardon his brother, but threw him into prison, that is, he wanted the destruction of his own soul and his eternal torment.

18.19.0.en: When his fellow servants saw this, who represent the Church, they were greatly grieved, so they prayed for the second servant who was thrown into prison.

18.19.1.en: And the king, that is, God, heard from the Church, and summoned the first servant and rebuked him severely for his cruelty, and for not appreciating the divine forgiveness granted to him, and his cruelty in not forgiving his brother. And he commanded that he be thrown into prison, to pay all that was due until the last farthing of all his debts. What is meant is that he remains in prison, that is, in torment forever, because of his not forgiving the one who sinned against him, since he will not be able to pay this unlimited debt.

18.20.0.en: Christ affirms at the end of the parable that what is meant by it is God's not forgiving the one who does not forgive others. And He said "my Father", because the one who does not forgive others does not deserve to call God his Father, so He did not say "your Father". Offer your repentance every day before God, confident of His forgiveness, so that your repentance is joined with much thanksgiving. And as you strive to correct your faults, God supports you and your thanks to Him increases, and then you will be compassionate toward those who wrong you because they are sick like you, in need of divine forgiveness and the healing medicine from it. So do not be troubled by them, because your sins against God are greater, but pray for yourself and for them, and the mercies of God will embrace you all.
